subject: Q3 Strategy & OKRs — leadership alignment and sign-off
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc:

Subject: Q3 Strategy & OKRs — leadership alignment and sign-off

Team,

We're starting Q3 OKR sign-off. Attached is Q3_OKR_Draft_v3.xlsx — it's the compiled draft from product, eng, and go-to-market. I summarized the key asks below so leadership can sign off by EOD Thursday PST: 

- Company-level objective + 3 key results (revenue-mix, latency P95, platform reliability).
- Cross-functional KR owners and rollup method (how teams report progress).
- One stretch initiative for cost-per-inference reduction and one for quality (eval/regression).

Please review the sheet and call out any blockers or material changes you want before sign-off. If you have metric objections, mark them as comments in the sheet and reply here with a short justification.

Prep notes: we'll use this for the QBR narrative next week — Marta from Venture Analytics will help run the external view. I attached the draft QBR agenda as well.

Action items:
- By Thu 17 Mar 2026 17:00 PST: final comments in-sheet or email.
- By Fri 18 Mar 2026 10:00 PST: leadership sign-off thread closed.

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
VP, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Q3 Strategy & OKRs — leadership alignment and sign-off

Laura — quick read-through. High-level: looks solid. Two asks from Eng that I want to surface before we lock:

1) Latency KR: current draft calls for P95 <= 120ms for hosted tier. Our telemetry shows baseline at 145ms for peak sequences; with proposed batching changes we can get to ~130ms but 120ms is optimistic. Recommend we set phased KRs: 130ms by end of Q3 and 120ms as a stretch/bonus KR.

2) Cost-per-inference KR: the target assumes quantization rollout across models in the catalog. We should tie that KR to specific models (e.g., m-3b, m-7b) and include a rollout schedule. Otherwise the metric is not actionable.

I'll add comments to the spreadsheet and flag owners. If leadership prefers, we can keep the high-level numbers and add an engineering caveat in the QBR narrative.

— Markus
Director of Engineering, Serving Runtime
markus_klein@redwood.ai

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Q3 Strategy & OKRs — leadership alignment and sign-off

Thanks Markus — +1 on making the latency KR phased. From GTM perspective, I also want to ensure the revenue KR reflects a mix signal (hosted vs dedicated vs private). The current topline goal is fine but we should have a measurable expansion KR for Dedicated (reserved capacity) — recommend: +25% committed monthly spend from top 20 accounts (YoY).

I've added a few rows to the spreadsheet: revenue mix, dedicated expansion, and a single Net Revenue Retention (NRR) target. These are marked with owners (Priyom for enterprise sales, Monica for CS).

Also flagged the QBR agenda item "Pricing & Contracting levers" — we should have a short decision list for any pricing experiments we want to greenlight in Q3.

-Aisha
Head of Growth & GTM Operations
aisha_rahman@redwood.ai

From: Marta Ruiz <mruiz@ventureanalytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 14:20:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Q3 Strategy & OKRs — leadership alignment and sign-off

Hi Laura & team — thanks for sharing. I'm the external analyst joining for QBR prep. I reviewed the draft and attached a short facilitation note in the folder (see QBR prep doc in Drive). Two observations from an investor/board perspective:

- They will want to see clear leading indicators for revenue that tie to product usage (e.g., per-customer inference volume growth for top accounts). If you can add a lead indicator row, it helps the narrative.
- For reliability/latency: show risk and mitigation. If latency is a stretch KR, include a short mitigation plan (fallback model variants, routing policy).

I've proposed a 90-minute QBR flow in the attached agenda (QBR_agenda_v2.pdf): 15m exec summary, 25m GTM performance, 20m Product & Reliability, 20m Roadmap decisions, 10m action sign-off.

I'll be available Thursday afternoon to run a dry run if helpful.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Senior Analyst, Venture Analytics
